name: AI Engineer Roadmap
tagline: From Python and the math behind models to shipping reliable LLM-powered products
summary: An ordered path for engineers who turn models into products. It starts with Python, the mathematics and data skills models depend on, moves through machine learning, deep learning and transformers, then into the applied layer — prompting, embeddings, retrieval — and finally into the backend and operations work that makes an AI feature fast, affordable, observable and safe in production.

steps.label: Python & programming fundamentals
steps.note: Python is the language of every ML library and most serving code; fluency with data structures and packaging comes before any model.

steps.label: Linear algebra, probability & statistics
steps.note: Vectors, matrices, gradients and distributions are what embeddings, loss functions and evaluation metrics are made of.

steps.label: Data handling (SQL & pandas)
steps.note: Most of an AI project is finding, cleaning and joining data; SQL and dataframes are how you do that before a single model runs.

steps.label: Machine learning fundamentals
steps.note: Train/test splits, overfitting, regularisation and metrics are the mental model you will reuse when evaluating LLM outputs.

steps.label: Deep learning & neural networks
steps.note: Backpropagation, optimisers and GPUs explain why models cost what they cost and why inference latency behaves the way it does.

steps.label: Transformers & large language models
steps.note: Attention, tokenisation and context windows are the constraints behind every prompt, cost estimate and truncation bug you will meet.

steps.label: Prompt engineering & structured output
steps.note: Instructions, few-shot examples, tool schemas and JSON mode are the cheapest levers for quality and the first thing to master in production.

steps.label: Embeddings & vector search
steps.note: Turning text into vectors and searching by similarity is the mechanism behind retrieval, deduplication and semantic caching.

steps.label: Search & vector stores
steps.note: A search engine with keyword, filter and vector (kNN) queries gives hybrid retrieval; learn one store and its indexing trade-offs.

steps.label: Retrieval-augmented generation
steps.note: RAG combines everything so far — chunking, embeddings, retrieval, prompting — into the architecture most LLM products actually ship.

steps.label: HTTP & REST APIs
steps.note: Models are consumed over HTTP; request/response contracts, timeouts and status codes decide whether the feature feels reliable.

steps.label: Backend service for inference
steps.note: A stateless service wraps the model call with validation, auth and retries; this is where an experiment becomes an endpoint.

steps.label: Streaming responses (SSE)
steps.note: Token-by-token streaming hides multi-second latency from users; Server-Sent Events is the simplest protocol that delivers it.

steps.label: Caching & semantic caching
steps.note: Model calls are slow and billed per token, so caching identical or semantically similar prompts is the first big cost win.

steps.label: Rate limiting & cost control
steps.note: Provider quotas and per-user budgets must be enforced before launch; otherwise one loop or one abusive client drains the bill.

steps.label: Async pipelines & batch jobs
steps.note: Embedding millions of documents or re-indexing nightly does not belong in a request; queues and workers make ingestion reliable.

steps.label: Docker & model packaging
steps.note: Pinning CUDA, library and model versions in an image is the only way inference behaves the same in staging and production.

steps.label: Model serving & GPU infrastructure
steps.note: Batching, quantisation and GPU scheduling decide throughput and cost when you host models yourself instead of calling an API.

steps.label: LLM observability & evaluation
steps.note: Tracing prompts, tokens, latency and quality scores per request is how you catch regressions that unit tests cannot express.

steps.label: Guardrails, safety & privacy
steps.note: Input filtering, output validation, PII handling and prompt-injection defences are launch blockers, not polish.

steps.label: Fine-tuning & model adaptation
steps.note: Only after prompting and retrieval plateau does fine-tuning pay off; knowing the evaluation loop first keeps it honest.

steps.label: Agents & tool use
steps.note: Multi-step agents that call tools reuse every skill above — APIs, retries, idempotency, observability — with the model as the planner.
